scope: Independent evidence relevant to the March 18 shipping-fuel -> freight -> food-cost transmission hypothesis

observations: As of March 11, Global 20 Ports VLSFO averaged $960 per metric ton, up 79% from two weeks earlier.
IFO 380 reached an all-time high of $886 per metric ton on March 9 and was $794 on March 11.
U.S. Gulf-to-Japan grain ocean freight was $58 per metric ton as of March 5, up 6% week over week and 16% from the first available rate of the year.
Pacific Northwest-to-Japan grain ocean freight was $33 per metric ton, up 6% week over week and 25% from the first available rate of the year.
March final-demand energy rose 8.5% month over month.
No. 2 diesel fuel in processed intermediate demand rose 42.0% month over month.
Final-demand transportation and warehousing services rose 1.3% month over month.
Truck transportation of freight moved higher in March.
Processed foods and feeds rose 0.9% month over month even while final-demand foods fell 0.3%.
USDA states diesel fuel price is a proxy for trends in U.S. truck rates because diesel is a significant expense for grain movements.
U.S. average diesel price in Q1 2026 was $4.12 per gallon, up 11% from the previous quarter and 14% from the same quarter a year earlier.
June BNSF fuel surcharge was scheduled to rise to $0.46 per mile from $0.08 in June 2025.
June Union Pacific fuel surcharge was scheduled to rise to $0.69 per mile from $0.30 in June 2025.
For Wichita-to-Houston shipments, the June 2025 to June 2026 fuel-surcharge rise translated to about $387 more per BNSF car and $251 more per UP car.

mechanism_graph: consumer food-price transmission subject to lag, margins, inventories, commodity prices, and substitution
anti_overclaim_rules: The evidence establishes several intermediate links in the proposed mechanism but does not establish that shipping fuel was the sole or dominant cause of later consumer food inflation.
Food commodity prices, weather, inventories, labor, exchange rates, tariffs, margins, and demand remain independent transition elements.
A lagged food-price effect must be tested against predeclared windows rather than selected after observing CPI outcomes.
The March 18 Randolph source itself must be fully preserved before its exact mechanism strength and timing can be scored.
